model_annotation: This bar chart, titled "Durchschnitte in %", illustrates average percentage values for four economic indicators across three decades: the 2000s, 2010s, and 2020s. The horizontal axis presents these three time periods as categorical groupings, while the vertical axis, labeled "Durchschnitte in %", displays values on a linear scale ranging from -2.0% to 6.0%, with tick marks every 1.0 unit. Within each decade, four bars are grouped together, each representing a different indicator: "Welt-BIP" (global GDP) shown in green, "Exporte Deutschland" (German exports) in dark blue, "Welthandel" (global trade) in light green, and "Industrieproduktion Deutschland" (German industrial production) in light blue. For the 2000s, the bars show values of 3.9% (Welt-BIP), 5.4% (Welthandel), 5.3% (Exporte Deutschland), and 1.0% (Industrieproduktion Deutschland). In the 2010s, the values are 3.7% (Welt-BIP), 4.8% (Welthandel), 5.0% (Exporte Deutschland), and 2.2% (Industrieproduktion Deutschland). For the 2020s, the values are 2.7% (Welt-BIP), 2.3% (Welthandel), 0.4% (Exporte Deutschland), and -1.5% (Industrieproduktion Deutschland), with the last bar extending below the zero line. The bars are not sorted by height but are presented in the order specified by the legend, which groups them by indicator rather than by value.
